title: Finitely generated submodules of finite free modules over semihereditary rings
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring such that every finitely generated ideal of $R$ is projective [def-weil-pbc-projective-module]. For every integer $n\geq0$ and every finitely generated $R$-submodule $K\subseteq R^n$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], the $R$-module $K$ is projective.

source.place: Lemma 6.7(1), algebraic sublemma making explicit the finite projective resolution assertion; extracted by the worker. This general finite-submodule assertion is not quoted as an exact Stacks theorem.

proof.text: Fix $R$ satisfying the stated ideal hypothesis. We prove by induction on $n$ that every finitely generated submodule of $R^n$ is projective. For $n=0$, every submodule is the zero module. Every linear map from the zero module lifts along every surjection by the zero map, so the lifting characterization in [def-weil-pbc-projective-module] proves the base case.

source.place: Tags 05CE (definition-projective) and 05CF (lemma-characterize-projective); elementary rank induction written by ND, not asserted to be the statement of either tag.

proof.text: Assume the claim at rank $n$, and let $K\subseteq R^{n+1}$ have generators $k_1,\ldots,k_r$ as in [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Let $p:K\to R$ be the last coordinate. Its image $I=p(K)$ is an ideal: sums and scalar multiples of images are images. It is generated by $p(k_1),\ldots,p(k_r)$, since applying $p$ to $k=\sum_j a_jk_j$ gives $p(k)=\sum_j a_jp(k_j)$. Thus the hypothesis on $R$ makes $I$ projective [def-weil-pbc-projective-module].

source.place: Tags 05CE (definition-projective) and 05CF (lemma-characterize-projective); elementary rank induction written by ND, not asserted to be the statement of either tag.

proof.text: Regard $p$ as a surjection $K\to I$. Apply the lifting characterization in [def-weil-pbc-projective-module] to $\mathrm{id}_I:I\to I$ and this surjection. It gives an $R$-linear map $s:I\to K$ with $ps=\mathrm{id}_I$.

source.place: Tags 05CE (definition-projective) and 05CF (lemma-characterize-projective); elementary rank induction written by ND, not asserted to be the statement of either tag.

proof.text: Put $L=\ker(p)$ and $q:K\to L$, $q(k)=k-s(p(k))$. Indeed $p(q(k))=p(k)-ps(p(k))=0$, and $q(l)=l$ for $l\in L$. If $l=\sum_j a_jk_j$, then $l=q(l)=\sum_j a_jq(k_j)$. Thus $q(k_1),\ldots,q(k_r)$ generate $L$ in the sense of [def-weil-finitely-generated-module]. Deleting the last coordinate identifies $L$ linearly with a submodule $L_0\subseteq R^n$; the inverse appends a zero coordinate. The images of these generators generate $L_0$.

source.place: Tags 05CE (definition-projective) and 05CF (lemma-characterize-projective); elementary rank induction written by ND, not asserted to be the statement of either tag.

proof.text: The induction hypothesis applies to the finitely generated submodule $L_0\subseteq R^n$ and makes it projective. Therefore $L$ is projective as well: for any surjection and any map from $L$, compose the map with $L_0\to L$, lift using projectivity of $L_0$, and compose the lift with $L\to L_0$. This is exactly the lifting characterization in [def-weil-pbc-projective-module].

source.place: Tags 05CE (definition-projective) and 05CF (lemma-characterize-projective); elementary rank induction written by ND, not asserted to be the statement of either tag.

proof.text: To prove projectivity of $K$ directly, let $t:A\to B$ be any surjective $R$-linear map and $u:K\to B$ any $R$-linear map. By [def-weil-pbc-projective-module], projectivity of $L$ and $I$ gives lifts $v_L:L\to A$ and $v_I:I\to A$ with $tv_L=u|_L$ and $tv_I=us$. Define $v(k)=v_L(q(k))+v_I(p(k))$. This map is linear and $tv(k)=u(k-s(p(k)))+u(s(p(k)))=u(k)$. Hence every such $u$ lifts, so $K$ is projective. This proves the induction step and the assertion for all $n\geq0$.

source.place: Tags 05CE (definition-projective) and 05CF (lemma-characterize-projective); elementary rank induction written by ND, not asserted to be the statement of either tag.
